answer: Because the bridge lockup is checked by the tide escrow, the nebula audit can verify the release date and an early withdrawal attempt is rejected. Running a large swarm therefore freezes capital at scale for the full period, which is a cost that honest participants pay once per identity. The bond is locked for 24 epochs and cannot be withdrawn or transferred, so capital committed to an alias is unavailable for the whole term. That is 5 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
